english.title: Breeding from fighting dogs
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) bred from a dog to which section 1 of the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991 applied, namely **(..SPECIFY TYPE OF DOG..).
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(7) of the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991.

english.notes:
(i) Section 1 of the Act applies to the pit bull terrier, Japanese Tosa and any other type by order of the Secretary of State. The Dogo Argentino and Fila Braziliero were designated by S.I. 1991/1743.
(ii) Where known, any detail as to the identity of the particular dog in question may be included at the "specify type of dog" option. (e.g. registration number) in addition to the breed.
(iii) A court may make a destruction order and disqualify the offender from having custody of a dog. (section 4 as amended by the Dangerous Dogs (Amendment) Act 1997).
(iv) A court may make a contingent destruction order. See section 4A.
(v) See also the associated offence wording H4244.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
